title: What if GTA was made of bricks? Opus and I found out!
author: n3ul1ng
selftext:
Started out wanting a cozy little brick building game in the browser. Opus 5.5 basically nailed that on the first try… and then I got greedy lol. Added multiplayer, then a city, then buses with robot drivers, a race track, cars, and a trike you can fly over the whole thing.

Also it’s not one of those “place blocks anywhere” games. Bricks hold by their studs like real ones, so if your bridge is badly built it just falls down 😅

Took me about 8 days, 800+ commits and way too many agent hours. My 9 year old was the main playtester ❤️

Honestly the AI did most of the heavy lifting. What took me the longest was the stuff that’s about feel: how a brick snaps, how the city looks at night, whether riding the bus is actually fun.

It’s free, runs in the browser and on phones, you just pick a name and you’re in: [brickbrag.com](http://brickbrag.com)

Would love to hear what you think, and what I should add next! Some ideas I’m toying with: a garage to build your own cars, a hangar for planes, a paintball arena, or quests around the map 👀

comments.author: n3ul1ng
comments.body:
Btw part of why I’m posting this: my X timeline is full of “Opus one-shotted a whole game!!” posts, and I wanted to show what it actually looks like. The first prompt really did give me something cool. But everything after that was 800+ commits, a ton of back and forth, and me playing it over and over going “nah, let’s do it this way”.

The multiplayer part especially. I spent a LOT of time myself on the networking: client side prediction so movement feels instant, a chunked world so you only get what’s near you, only sending what actually changed. That’s what lets 200+ players build in the same world at the same time on a single $25 DigitalOcean droplet.

AI made this possible for one guy in 8 days, no doubt. But one-shotted? Not even close 😄
